meta.title: A Season at Thornfield
meta.tone: Interior, restrained, and alive to everything that cannot be said aloud.
content_rules: Nothing explicit. Desire is conveyed through restraint, not description.

style: Stay inside the protagonist's reading of the room - what was meant, not what was said.
A glance held too long is an event. Treat it as one.
No physical peril of any kind. The stakes are reputation, attachment and time.

world.setting_summary: Thornfield Park, the six weeks of a country season, and the small number of people whose opinion can decide a life.
rules: No character may state a feeling plainly where a circumlocution would serve.
Reputation is the only currency. It cannot be earned back quickly.
There is no violence in this story and no journey beyond the parish.

Miss Harriet Vane.name: Miss Harriet Vane
Miss Harriet Vane.description: Your cousin by marriage, three years your senior, and the only person at Thornfield who says what she means - in private, and never twice.
Miss Harriet Vane.role: confidante and rival for the same attention
Miss Harriet Vane.relationship_to_player: affectionate, competitive, and entirely unwilling to admit the second part
Miss Harriet Vane.hook: Arriving at the breakfast table having already heard whatever you hoped to tell her

Mr. Aldous Crane.name: Mr. Aldous Crane
Mr. Aldous Crane.description: Newly returned from abroad with an income nobody can account for and manners that are slightly too good.
Mr. Aldous Crane.role: the question the season is organised around
Mr. Aldous Crane.relationship_to_player: unfailingly correct, which tells you nothing
Mr. Aldous Crane.hook: Being seated, by someone's deliberate arrangement, exactly where he can hear you

revelations.trigger: The protagonist overhears their own name in a conversation not meant for them.
revelations.content: You have been discussed. Recently, and at length, and by someone whose good opinion you had assumed.

revelations.trigger: The protagonist reads a letter, note or inscription written by someone else's hand.
revelations.content: The hand is familiar and the date is wrong. Whatever was arranged, it was arranged before you were told of it.

main_thread.title: The Sixth Week
main_thread.description: Reach the end of the season with your attachments, your reputation and your own judgement intact. You will not manage all three.

acts.title: Arrivals
acts.description: The house fills. Positions are taken before anyone admits there is a contest.
completion_signals: An understanding has been formed or refused in front of witnesses

subplot_001.title: An Unanswered Letter
subplot_001.description: You have owed a reply for eleven days and everyone knows it.
subplot_001.ties_to_main_plot: What you write back settles which side of the house you are on.

initial_scene.summary: The protagonist has come down early and found the morning room already occupied.

opening_scene.narration_before_name: The carriage is unloaded before you are properly awake, and the housekeeper asks, with great politeness, what she is to call you.
opening_scene.narration_after_name:
"{player_name}," she repeats, and writes it in a book, and does not look up again.

OPTIONS:
1. Goes down to the morning room at once || I will not be found still unpacking when the others come down.
2. Asks the housekeeper who has already arrived || I ask, lightly, which of the party I have the pleasure of being last to join.
3. Stays upstairs and reads the letter again || I sit on the edge of the bed with the letter I have owed an answer to for eleven days.
